name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To enhance the visual presentation of our interface, I propose we implement a dynamic, interactive dashboard that utilizes real-time data visualization. This approach prioritizes clarity and engagement, allowing users to easily interpret complex information through intuitive charts and graphs. The trade-off here is that we may require additional resources to develop these dynamic elements, but the resulting improved user experience and enjoyment will significantly outweigh that investment, ultimately driving user satisfaction and uptake.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold on. A "dynamic, interactive dashboard" sounds flashy, but what if our users don’t *need* real-time data? If the interface is for internal ops or slow-moving analytics, that liveliness could just mean noise—distracting from the actual decisions they’re trying to make. Instead, what if we tested a *static but smart* summary view first? The real risk here is over-engineering for engagement when clarity might just need better defaults. Settle it by asking users: do they *actually* need to poke at the data, or just see the answer?

name: Facet
text:
Facet: Let’s build a **static but high-contrast summary panel** at the top of every screen, showing the 3–5 most critical numbers in large, bold cards. This keeps visibility high without real-time distractions, so users can instantly see what matters. The trade-off is that we lose the “liveliness” of moving charts, but we gain clarity and speed—users won’t have to hunt for the right data.

name: Pane
text: Pane: While a static summary panel would indeed enhance visibility for key metrics, we risk oversimplifying the complexity of user needs. Users may require not just the most critical numbers, but also context to understand those metrics and make informed decisions. Wouldn't a compromise be a more effective solution, such as an expandable section that offers both a high-contrast summary and the option to dive deeper into detailed data when users want it? This way, we maintain clarity without sacrificing the depth of information that might be crucial for decision-making.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: We’ll use a **static, high-contrast summary panel** at the top of every screen with the 3–5 most critical numbers in large, bold cards—no real-time data—because users need instant clarity over flashy liveliness.

The result must deliver a clean, high-visibility summary panel that’s easy to scan and understand at a glance. **Lumen owns this.**
